reason: This book already reflects the correct read of the current macro backdrop and changing it now would just pay friction for no new edge. Research into the last few days confirms the Fed held a hawkish line after the 2026-09-16 FOMC: two-year Treasury yields are at their highest since mid-2024, the 10-year is near 5%, the dollar index is firm around 99.9 and pushing higher against the yen after a hawkish BOJ dissent, and Indian government bonds have now fallen for a fifth straight week on the combined pressure of Fed tightening and RBI positioning -- exactly the environment that argues for staying diversified across EM/Asia (EEM, TSM, EWJ, INDA, EWZ) with modest per-name size (8-10% each), a standing US inverse hedge (SQQQ) against a domestic drawdown, tight stops (-8% to -20%) on every leg, and a large 46% cash buffer rather than pressing risk. The book is already up +2.16% since inception despite the hawkish FOMC because the stops and sizing did their job (EEM +1.99%, TSM +4.06%, INDA +1.18%, EWZ flat), and the SQQQ hedge is behaving as insurance is supposed to (modestly underwater at -6.75% while the rest of the book, and the broader tape, hasn't cracked). Nothing in the last three days -- no new Fed communication, no EM-specific shock, no move that breaches any stop -- changes that thesis; a full replacement here would just realize 2bps-per-side churn costs across six legs to arrive at a substantially similar risk posture. The disciplined move is to let the existing stops and take-profits do their job and reassess after the next real information event (next FOMC-adjacent data or a stop trigger), not to trade for the sake of trading.
